resources.string: Lets AutoClique Live tap the screen at the points you marked. No screen content is read or sent off the device.
Before you start, read how the app works

AutoClique Live taps the screen for you, at the points and intervals you configure yourself. It only follows what you set up: it makes no decisions on its own, does not learn and does not change its behavior by itself.\n\nTo do that it needs two sensitive permissions. Here is exactly what each one does.

It is the only way on Android for an app to tap the screen of another app. AutoClique Live uses it only to perform taps at the coordinates you marked.\n\nIt does not read text, buttons, passwords or any content of the screens you use. The service ignores every accessibility event the system sends.

Used only if you enable “Tap only when the color matches” on a point. In that case the app reads the pixel color at that coordinate to know whether the button you want has appeared.\n\nNo image is recorded, displayed or stored. Only the color value at that point is compared, in memory, and discarded right after. If you don\'t use the color trigger, this permission is never requested.
What the app does not do

• Does not collect, store or share personal data.
• Sends nothing to the internet: the app does not request network permission, so it has no way to transmit anything.
• Shows no ads and uses no analytics tools.
• Your settings (points, intervals and colors) stay on this device only and are deleted when you uninstall.
I accept and want to continue
How to enable the Accessibility permission

Android will open the Accessibility settings. Do this:

1. Find AutoClique Live in the list. On some phones it is under “Installed apps” or “Downloaded apps”.
2. Tap it and switch it on.
3. Confirm the warning Android shows and come back here.

This is AutoClique's own service, not TalkBack or the screen reader — you don't need to turn those on. The service only performs the taps you configured; it does not read the screen.
